annotations.proposed_function: Stabilizes the interaction with RNA by reducing the dissociation rate (off-rate) of the Mmi1 YTH domain-RNA complex.
annotations.evidence: When we analyzed RNA binding by EMSA using this construct, a stable RNA-protein complex was visualized as a better-defined band on the gel (Fig. 1B, right).
annotations.curator_note: Exact positions given (residues 282-326 defined as USR); experimental binding to RNA confirmed via EMSA and kinetics.

annotations.evidence: We previously showed that the first 50 amino acids of Mmi1 contain a low-complexity region that is critical for binding Ccr4-Not (10).
annotations.curator_note: Exact positions given (first 50 amino acids); binding partner Ccr4-Not specified.

annotations.proposed_function: Folds back to contact the back of the YTH domain, forming a network of hydrophobic interactions involving residues L316, F318, and H324.
annotations.evidence: In summary, our structure shows that part of the low-complexity USR of Mmi1 (residues 315– 326) lacks secondary structure elements but adopts a defined fold on RNA-binding, forming contacts with the YTH domain.
annotations.curator_note: Exact positions given (315-326) and specific binding partners (YTH domain residues) identified in crystal structure.

annotations.proposed_function: Contributes to the interaction with RNA via stabilizing the conformation and reducing the flexibility of the N-clamp in solution.
annotations.evidence: These data are consistent with the USR contributing to the interaction with RNA via stabilizing the conformation, and reducing the flexibility of the N-clamp in solution.
annotations.curator_note: Functional role in RNA binding is described, but specific numerical coordinates for the USR region involved in this specific stabilization effect are not explicitly stated in this sentence (though 315-326 is mentioned elsewhere for protein-protein contacts).

annotations.proposed_function: Stabilizes the conformation of the YTH domain to enhance RNA binding affinity; contributes structurally to the interaction with DSR RNA.
annotations.evidence: Here, we show that stable RNA binding by Mmi1 is dependent not only on its YTH domain but also on an upstream low-complexity region (residues 282–346).
annotations.curator_note: Exact positions given and experimental binding evidence (truncation assays/NMR) provided.

annotations.proposed_function: Indirectly contributes to RNA binding by stabilizing the conformation of the N- and C-clamps of the YTH domain.
annotations.evidence: Within the low-complexity region, the USR (residues 282–326) likely contributes to RNA binding indirectly.
annotations.curator_note: Exact positions given. Function is indirect stabilization rather than direct contact, but binding impact is experimentally verified.

annotations.proposed_function: Stabilizes a conformation of the YTH domain that binds RNA with high affinity
annotations.evidence: In the case of Mmi1, the USR stabilizes a conformation of the YTH domain that binds RNA with high affinity.
annotations.curator_note: Qualitative mention of USR function; specific residue coordinates for the USR are not provided in this text segment.

annotations.proposed_function: Induces allosteric changes in the DNA binding domain to enhance DNA binding
annotations.evidence: For example, an IDR in the glucocorticoid receptor induces allosteric changes in the DNA binding domain to enhance DNA binding, likely by stabilizing a high affinity conformation (44).
annotations.curator_note: Qualitative mention of IDR function; specific residue coordinates are not provided.

annotations.proposed_function: Increases the affinity of interaction of the Mmi1 YTH domain with RNA and slows the off-rate of the YTH domain for RNA.
annotations.evidence: The USR increases the affinity of interaction of the Mmi1 YTH domain with RNA.
annotations.curator_note: Exact positions given (282-327) derived from construct definitions in Table 1 and Figure 1A; experimental binding to RNA confirmed via EMSA and fluorescence polarization.

annotations.proposed_function: Enhances high-affinity binding to DSR RNA by slowing the off-rate and stabilizing the RNA-bound conformation.
annotations.evidence: Figure 4. A network of interactions is formed between the USR, N-clamp, and core YTH domain. (A) Co-crystal structure of Mmi1 USR-YTH (residues 315–488 modelled) with DSR RNA. Cartoon representation shows protein in blue and RNA in yellow. The USR is shown in darker blue. (B) The conformation of the USR is stabilized by hydrophobic contacts with the core YTH domain and N-clamp. Residues labelled in turquoise either appear or show large chemical shift changes on RNA binding in NMR experiments (see Fig. 5).
annotations.curator_note: Exact positions given (315-326) in Figure 4 legend and diagram; experimental binding to DSR RNA confirmed via co-crystal structure and kinetics.
